newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gives guarantees to private electric firms.
newsitem.headline: Mexico gives guarantees to private electric firms.

text.p: Mexico has created a system of guarantees to protect private generators and distributors of electricity for domestic use, the Energy Ministry said Tuesday.
The government drew up the rules in response to concerns from private companies worried by potential unfair competition from the government.
The country has begun opening up the distribution of electricity to private companies, removing exclusive control from the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE).
Mexico also is privatizing natural gas distribution, formerly the domain of state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
"The accords aim to give transparency and certainty to electric energy generation projects," the ministry said in a statement.
The statement also said the rules will more clearly define the interconnection process with the government's grid.

Mexico is scheduled to open technical and economic bids for the long-delayed Merida III thermoelectric power project later this week. The results of bidding to operate the 440 Mw plant, scheduled to come on line in 2000, will be announced by the end of the month, a CFE spokesman said.
